headline: Over 50 injured as Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash across 3 Dhaka campuses
summary: Violent clashes erupted at Jagannath University, Dhaka College, and Govt Madrasa-e-Alia, marking the largest confrontation between the two student wings since the July uprising.
details: Clashes broke out on Tuesday at Jagannath University, Dhaka College, and Govt Madrasa-e-Alia, leaving more than 50 activists injured. The violence continued until evening, following similar clashes at Begum Rokeya University in Rangpur on Monday.
caption:
More than 50 injured as violence returns to campuses. Chhatra Dal and Shibir clash across three major institutions in Dhaka.

Clashes broke out on Tuesday at Jagannath University, Dhaka College, and Govt Madrasa-e-Alia, leaving more than 50 activists injured. The violence continued until evening, following similar clashes at Begum Rokeya University in Rangpur on Monday.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: [[6 Naya Dhara leaders in custody]] after Press Club clash and DMCH standoff
headline: 6 Naya Dhara leaders in custody after Press Club clash and DMCH standoff
summary: Police detained several leaders following a violent clash between Naya Dhara and Rashtra Sanglap Forum that disrupted emergency services at Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
details: Police took six leaders and activists of Naya Dhara Bangladesh into custody Tuesday night. The action followed a clash with members of the Rashtra Sanglap Forum near the Jatiya Press Club and a subsequent three-hour standoff at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).

The detainees include Naya Dhara Chairman Momin Mehedi, Senior Vice-Chairman Shanta Farzana, Vice-Chairman Dr Nurjahan Nira, Joint Secretary General Monir Zaman, and organising secretaries Atap Mondal and Haridas Sarkar.

The conflict began Tuesday evening during a Naya Dhara programme protesting an alleged assault on Shanta Farzana. The clash left several people injured from both sides, including Shanta and Rashtra Sanglap Forum Member Secretary ANM Ayas, who were taken to DMCH for treatment.

At the hospital, supporters of the Rashtra Sanglap Forum allegedly confined Naya Dhara leaders inside the emergency department for three hours. The disorder disrupted critical medical services for approximately one and a half hours, causing fear among patients and attendants.

The two groups provided conflicting accounts of the incident. Rashtra Sanglap Forum claimed Naya Dhara activists attacked them after offensive remarks were made about July fighters and the BNP, while Naya Dhara alleged that Ayas and his group initiated the attack and stole journalists' phones.
